001package io.jstach.rainbowgum;
002
003import java.io.PrintStream;
004import java.lang.System.Logger.Level;
005import java.time.Instant;
006import java.util.ArrayList;
007import java.util.Arrays;
008import java.util.List;
009import java.util.Locale;
010import java.util.Objects;
011import java.util.concurrent.CopyOnWriteArrayList;
012import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;
013import java.util.concurrent.locks.ReentrantLock;
014import java.util.function.Supplier;
015
016import org.jspecify.annotations.Nullable;
017
018/**
019 * Alerts (sometimes called errors or status events elsewhere) are for reporting problems
020 * with the logging system itself rather than application logging - for example an
021 * appender failing to write, or an async publisher's queue overflowing. Because logging
022 * itself may be broken these are not routed through the normal {@link LogRouter} but are
023 * instead kept in a small in memory ring buffer (see {@link #dump()} and
024 * {@link #stats()}). Warning and error alerts are also reported immediately (currently to
025 * stderr); informational alerts remain available for diagnostics without producing output
026 * by default.
027 * <p>
028 * An instance is available from every {@link LogConfig#alerts()}. Components that are
029 * {@linkplain LogProvider provided} config, or that are
030 * {@linkplain LogLifecycle#start( LogConfig) started} with config, should prefer
031 * capturing {@code config.alerts()} over reaching for global state.
032 * <p>
033 * {@link LogAlerts} is itself a {@link LogLifecycle}: {@link #start(LogConfig)} is called
034 * exactly once, after every
035 * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} has run, and is
036 * where {@link UnobservedErrorsAction} (already resolved at construction, same as
037 * capacity) gets applied against whatever has been recorded by then - see that enum for
038 * what "nobody is listening yet" means and why it matters specifically at that moment
039 * rather than for the life of the process.
040 *
041 * @see LogConfig#alerts()
042 */
043public sealed interface LogAlerts extends LogLifecycle permits DefaultLogAlerts, SwappableLogAlerts {
044
045        /**
046         * Default capacity of the alert ring buffer.
047         */
048        static final int DEFAULT_CAPACITY = 512;
049
050        /**
051         * Records an alert.
052         * @param event event describing the alert.
053         */
054        public void alert(LogEvent event);
055
056        /**
057         * Records an alert.
058         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
059         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
060         */
061        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, Throwable throwable) {
062                String m = Objects.requireNonNullElse(throwable.getMessage(), "exception");
063                error(loggerName, m, throwable);
064        }
065
066        /**
067         * Records an alert.
068         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
069         * @param message alert message.
070         * @param throwable cause of the alert.
071         */
072        default void error(Class<?> loggerName, String message, Throwable throwable) {
073                alert(event(loggerName, Level.ERROR, message, throwable));
074        }
075
076        /**
077         * Records a warning alert.
078         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
079         * @param message alert message.
080         */
081        default void warn(Class<?> loggerName, String message) {
082                alert(event(loggerName, Level.WARNING, message, null));
083        }
084
085        /**
086         * Records an informational alert.
087         * @param loggerName usually the class where the alert originated.
088         * @param message alert message.
089         */
090        default void info(Class<?> loggerName, String message) {
091                alert(event(loggerName, Level.INFO, message, null));
092        }
093
094        private static LogEvent event(Class<?> loggerName, Level level, String message, @Nullable Throwable throwable) {
095                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
096                return LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), level,
097                                loggerName.getName(), message, KeyValues.of(), throwable);
098        }
099
100        /**
101         * A snapshot of the alerts currently held in the ring buffer, oldest first. Alerts
102         * are evicted oldest first once the buffer is at {@link Stats#capacity()}.
103         * @return immutable snapshot.
104         */
105        public List<LogEvent> dump();
106
107        /**
108         * Clears the ring buffer. Does not reset {@link Stats#total()} - like a
109         * Prometheus/Micrometer counter, that is meant to be monotonically increasing for the
110         * life of the process; a downstream metrics system computes rate of change rather
111         * than relying on the counter itself being reset.
112         */
113        public void clear();
114
115        /**
116         * Stats about the alerts recorded so far.
117         * @return stats.
118         */
119        public Stats stats();
120
121        /**
122         * Registers a listener that is notified synchronously, in addition to the alert being
123         * recorded in the ring buffer, every time {@link #alert(LogEvent)} is called.
124         * <p>
125         * <strong>Listeners are held with a normal (strong) reference and are not
126         * automatically removed.</strong> This is deliberate: alert listeners are expected to
127         * be few and long lived - typically registered once (e.g. a metrics bridge or an
128         * ops/paging integration) for as long as the owning {@link LogConfig} is - rather
129         * than one per short lived object. A weak reference would risk silently dropping a
130         * listener (a lambda with no other strong reference could be collected almost
131         * immediately) which is the wrong failure mode for something whose entire job is not
132         * losing alerts. Call {@link AutoCloseable#close()} on the returned registration to
133         * unregister deterministically once the caller's own lifecycle ends.
134         * @param listener listener to register.
135         * @return registration; {@link AutoCloseable#close()} unregisters the listener.
136         */
137        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener);
138
139        /**
140         * Notified of alerts as they happen. See {@link #addListener(Listener)}.
141         */
142        @FunctionalInterface
143        interface Listener {
144
145                /**
146                 * Called synchronously every time an alert is recorded. Should not throw -
147                 * exceptions are caught and reported separately so a broken listener cannot
148                 * disrupt alert recording or other listeners.
149                 * @param event the alert.
150                 */
151                void onAlert(LogEvent event);
152
153        }
154
155        /**
156         * Stats about alerts recorded.
157         *
158         * @param total total number of alerts ever recorded, including ones since evicted
159         * from the ring buffer.
160         * @param size number of alerts currently held in the ring buffer.
161         * @param capacity maximum number of alerts the ring buffer holds.
162         */
163        record Stats(long total, int size, int capacity) {
164        }
165
166        /**
167         * What {@link #start(LogConfig)} does if, at that moment, at least one error alert
168         * has been recorded and still zero {@link Listener}s are registered - the situation
169         * Logback's {@code StatusManager} calls an unobserved status: nothing is watching, so
170         * whatever went wrong during property loading or a
171         * {@link io.jstach.rainbowgum.spi.RainbowGumServiceProvider.Configurator} would
172         * otherwise only ever have reached the individual, easy to miss stderr lines each
173         * {@link #alert(LogEvent)} call already produces.
174         * <p>
175         * Deliberately keyed as
176         * {@value LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY} (an enum, not a
177         * boolean) since "fail" without "dump" first would throw away the only diagnostic
178         * evidence of why it failed.
179         */
180        enum UnobservedErrorsAction {
181
182                /**
183                 * Do nothing beyond the immediate reporting of warning and error events.
184                 */
185                NONE,
186                /**
187                 * Default. Report the whole backlog to {@code MetaLog} as one clearly labeled
188                 * block, the same way Logback auto-installs a console listener and prints its
189                 * accumulated status if nothing else is watching by the end of configuration -
190                 * RainbowGum still starts.
191                 */
192                DUMP,
193                /**
194                 * Same reporting as {@link #DUMP}, but then throws, so
195                 * {@link LogConfig.Builder#build()} (and therefore whatever is building a
196                 * {@link RainbowGum} from it) never completes. Goes further than Logback ever
197                 * does - an explicit, opt-in choice of integrity over resilience for deployments
198                 * where a silently-broken bootstrap is worse than refusing to start.
199                 */
200                FAIL;
201
202                static UnobservedErrorsAction parse(String value) {
203                        return LogProperty.enumValue(UnobservedErrorsAction.class, value);
204                }
205
206        }
207
208}
209
210/*
211 * Handed to PropertiesProviders. Buffers alerts until the configured LogAlerts exists,
212 * then drainTo replays the buffer into it and forwards every later call, so a provider
213 * may keep this instance and alert after provideProperties returns. Replay and swap
214 * happen under one lock so a concurrent alert is neither lost nor reordered. Listener
215 * registration is never supported: providers record alerts but cannot observe them.
216 */
217final class SwappableLogAlerts implements LogAlerts {
218
219        private final List<LogEvent> events = new ArrayList<>();
220
221        private long total;
222
223        private volatile @Nullable LogAlerts delegate;
224
225        @Override
226        public void alert(LogEvent event) {
227                var d = delegate;
228                if (d == null) {
229                        synchronized (this) {
230                                d = delegate;
231                                if (d == null) {
232                                        events.add(event.freeze());
233                                        total++;
234                                        return;
235                                }
236                        }
237                }
238                d.alert(event);
239        }
240
241        synchronized void drainTo(LogAlerts target) {
242                if (delegate != null) {
243                        throw new IllegalStateException("Alerts have already been drained");
244                }
245                for (var event : events) {
246                        target.alert(event);
247                }
248                events.clear();
249                delegate = target;
250        }
251
252        @Override
253        public synchronized List<LogEvent> dump() {
254                var d = delegate;
255                return d != null ? d.dump() : List.copyOf(events);
256        }
257
258        @Override
259        public synchronized void clear() {
260                var d = delegate;
261                if (d != null) {
262                        d.clear();
263                }
264                else {
265                        events.clear();
266                }
267        }
268
269        @Override
270        public synchronized Stats stats() {
271                var d = delegate;
272                return d != null ? d.stats() : new Stats(total, events.size(), Integer.MAX_VALUE);
273        }
274
275        @Override
276        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener) {
277                throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Properties providers cannot register alert listeners");
278        }
279
280        @Override
281        public void start(LogConfig config) {
282                throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Properties provider alerts cannot be started");
283        }
284
285        @Override
286        public synchronized void close() {
287                // The drained delegate belongs to LogConfig, so only an undrained buffer is
288                // dropped.
289                if (delegate == null) {
290                        events.clear();
291                }
292        }
293
294}
295
296final class DefaultLogAlerts implements LogAlerts {
297
298        private final LogEvent[] ring;
299
300        private int start = 0;
301
302        private int size = 0;
303
304        private final AtomicLong total = new AtomicLong();
305
306        private final AtomicLong errors = new AtomicLong();
307
308        private final ReentrantLock lock = new ReentrantLock();
309
310        private final CopyOnWriteArrayList<Listener> listeners = new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>();
311
312        /*
313         * Kept apart from listeners.isEmpty() deliberately: DefaultLogConfig's own
314         * metrics-bridge listener (see its constructor) is always registered before
315         * start(...) ever runs, and a passive in-process counter nobody has wired an exporter
316         * to is not "someone is watching" in the sense UnobservedErrorsAction cares about -
317         * only a real addListener(Listener) call (this class's public API) flips this.
318         */
319        private volatile boolean hasExternalListener = false;
320
321        private final LogEventFactory eventFactory = LogEventFactory.of(DefaultLogAlerts.class.getName());
322
323        /*
324         * Resolved once, at construction (same as capacity) rather than inside start(...):
325         * unlike capacity this does not shape any constructor-time state, but LogProperties
326         * is available just as early, and start(LogConfig) is really about announcing "I have
327         * started" (config is there because a few edge cases needed it, not because this
328         * needed to be a start-time lookup).
329         */
330        private final UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction;
331
332        /*
333         * Private and deliberately not defensive - of(LogProperties) below is the only
334         * caller, and it has already validated both fields (capacity > 0, a resolvable
335         * UnobservedErrorsAction) before ever reaching this constructor. Re-checking here
336         * would be defensive programming duplicating what was already a real, reported
337         * validation failure one call up - see of(...)'s own comment.
338         */
339        private DefaultLogAlerts(int capacity, UnobservedErrorsAction unobservedErrorsAction) {
340                this.ring = new LogEvent[capacity];
341                this.unobservedErrorsAction = unobservedErrorsAction;
342        }
343
344        /*
345         * Package-friend static factory: resolves and validates both
346         * LogProperties#ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY and
347         * LogProperties#ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY against one shared Validator
348         * - a mistake in both at once is reported together instead of only the first one
349         * found - then constructs. requirePositiveCapacity is a plain int -> int validating
350         * transform (not an object construction) specifically so it can sit inside map(...)
351         * without tripping CheckerFramework's Initialization Checker, which does not refine a
352         * `new Foo(...)` expression back to @Initialized when it appears directly inside a
353         * lambda body passed through a generic method like map(...) - the one and only `new
354         * DefaultLogAlerts(...)` call stays a plain, unconditional statement here instead.
355         */
356        static LogAlerts of(LogProperties properties) {
357                var validator = LogProperty.Validator.of(LogAlerts.class);
358                var unobservedErrorsActionResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY)
359                        .ofString()
360                        .map(UnobservedErrorsAction::parse)
361                        .or(UnobservedErrorsAction.DUMP)
362                        .validateIfError(validator);
363                var capacityResult = properties.forKey(LogProperties.ALERTS_CAPACITY_PROPERTY)
364                        .ofInt()
365                        .or(LogAlerts.DEFAULT_CAPACITY)
366                        .map(DefaultLogAlerts::requirePositiveCapacity)
367                        .validateIfError(validator);
368                validator.validate();
369                return new DefaultLogAlerts(capacityResult.value(), unobservedErrorsActionResult.value());
370        }
371
372        private static int requirePositiveCapacity(int capacity) {
373                if (capacity <= 0) {
374                        throw new IllegalArgumentException("capacity should be greater than 0");
375                }
376                return capacity;
377        }
378
379        @Override
380        public void alert(LogEvent event) {
381                var frozen = event.freeze();
382                total.incrementAndGet();
383                if (frozen.level() == Level.ERROR) {
384                        errors.incrementAndGet();
385                }
386                lock.lock();
387                try {
388                        if (size < ring.length) {
389                                ring[(start + size) % ring.length] = frozen;
390                                size++;
391                        }
392                        else {
393                                ring[start] = frozen;
394                                start = (start + 1) % ring.length;
395                        }
396                }
397                finally {
398                        lock.unlock();
399                }
400                for (var listener : listeners) {
401                        try {
402                                listener.onAlert(frozen);
403                        }
404                        catch (Exception e) {
405                                MetaLog.INSTANCE.log(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR, "LogAlerts.Listener threw", e));
406                        }
407                }
408                if (frozen.level() == Level.WARNING || frozen.level() == Level.ERROR) {
409                        MetaLog.INSTANCE.log(frozen);
410                }
411        }
412
413        @Override
414        public AutoCloseable addListener(Listener listener) {
415                listeners.add(listener);
416                hasExternalListener = true;
417                return () -> listeners.remove(listener);
418        }
419
420        /*
421         * DefaultLogConfig's own metrics-bridge listener goes through this instead of
422         * addListener(Listener) - see hasExternalListener's own comment for why.
423         */
424        void addInternalListener(Listener listener) {
425                listeners.add(listener);
426        }
427
428        @Override
429        public void start(LogConfig config) {
430                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.NONE || hasExternalListener || errors.get() == 0) {
431                        return;
432                }
433                var backlog = dump();
434                MetaLog.error(eventFactory.eventNoArg(Level.ERROR,
435                                backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered - "
436                                                + "dumping the backlog now since nothing else will see it:",
437                                null));
438                for (var event : backlog) {
439                        MetaLog.error(event);
440                }
441                if (unobservedErrorsAction == UnobservedErrorsAction.FAIL) {
442                        throw new IllegalStateException(
443                                        backlog.size() + " alert(s) were recorded before any LogAlerts.Listener was registered and "
444                                                        + LogProperties.ALERTS_UNOBSERVED_ERRORS_ACTION_PROPERTY + "=FAIL - refusing to start.");
445                }
446        }
447
448        @Override
449        public void close() {
450                listeners.clear();
451        }
452
453        @Override
454        public List<LogEvent> dump() {
455                lock.lock();
456                try {
457                        List<LogEvent> list = new ArrayList<>(size);
458                        for (int i = 0; i < size; i++) {
459                                var e = ring[(start + i) % ring.length];
460                                if (e != null) {
461                                        list.add(e);
462                                }
463                        }
464                        return List.copyOf(list);
465                }
466                finally {
467                        lock.unlock();
468                }
469        }
470
471        @Override
472        public void clear() {
473                lock.lock();
474                try {
475                        Arrays.fill(ring, null);
476                        start = 0;
477                        size = 0;
478                }
479                finally {
480                        lock.unlock();
481                }
482        }
483
484        @Override
485        public Stats stats() {
486                lock.lock();
487                try {
488                        return new Stats(total.get(), size, ring.length);
489                }
490                finally {
491                        lock.unlock();
492                }
493        }
494
495}
496
497/**
498 * Logging about logging. This is the static, always-available entry point used by code
499 * that cannot easily reach a {@link LogConfig} (e.g. before a {@link RainbowGum} is
500 * bound), and always reports directly (currently to stderr) rather than forwarding to a
501 * bound {@link RainbowGum}'s {@link LogConfig#alerts()} - alerts is a small bounded ring
502 * buffer meant to hold a curated, recent view of noteworthy logging-system problems, and
503 * {@link MetaLog} is used from enough different low level failure paths that routing it
504 * there risked flooding/evicting genuine alerts with whatever volume of things end up
505 * calling this class.
506 * <p>
507 * Components that already have (or can easily capture) a {@link LogConfig} - for example
508 * via {@link LogProvider} or {@link LogLifecycle#start(LogConfig)} - should prefer
509 * {@link LogConfig#alerts()} directly instead of this class.
510 *
511 * @author agentgt
512 */
513@SuppressWarnings("ImmutableEnumChecker")
514enum MetaLog implements LogEventLogger {
515
516        INSTANCE;
517
518        static Supplier<? extends @Nullable PrintStream> output = () -> System.err;
519
520        private final LogFormatter formatter = LogFormatter.builder() //
521                .text("[")
522                .level()
523                .text("] - RAINBOW_GUM")
524                .text(" - ")
525                .add(LogFormatter.of((b, e) -> {
526                        b.append(gumLoggerName(e.loggerName()));
527                }))
528                .text(" - ")
529                .message()
530                .textIfThrowable(" ")
531                .throwable()
532                .newline()
533                .build();
534
535        /**
536         * Reports a logging system event at its original level.
537         * @param event event to log.
538         */
539        static void error(LogEvent event) {
540                INSTANCE.log(event);
541        }
542
543        /**
544         * Logs an error in the logging system.
545         * @param loggerName derived from class.
546         * @param throwable error to log.
547         */
548        static void error(Class<?> loggerName, Throwable throwable) {
549                String m = Objects.requireNonNullElse(throwable.getMessage(), "exception");
550                error(loggerName, m, throwable);
551        }
552
553        /**
554         * Logs an error in the logging system.
555         * @param loggerName derived from class.
556         * @param message error message.
557         * @param throwable error to log.
558         */
559        static void error(Class<?> loggerName, String message, Throwable throwable) {
560                var currentThread = Thread.currentThread();
561                var event = LogEvent.of(Instant.now(), currentThread.getName(), currentThread.threadId(), Level.ERROR,
562                                loggerName.getName(), message, KeyValues.of(), throwable);
563                error(event);
564        }
565
566        private static String gumLoggerName(String value) {
567                String prefix = "io.jstach.rainbowgum.";
568                if (value.startsWith(prefix)) {
569                        value = value.substring(prefix.length());
570                }
571                return value;
572        }
573
574        @Override
575        public void log(LogEvent event) {
576                var err = output.get();
577                if (err != null) {
578                        var sb = new StringBuilder();
579                        formatter.format(sb, event);
580                        err.append(sb);
581                }
582        }
583
584}
